origin: Under Opus 5 the gap pass returned a fresh double-digit batch every cycle and every finding was approved — with auto on, an approval is what happens when nothing stops, and the specification grew by rules nobody decided. The record bar cuts `settled` back to what the record determines and gives the rest a lane: a product-level fork more than one answer fits is a `decide`, held out of the per-finding walk, put to the user as one scannable veto batch, and landed in the source document that should own the decision before the specification re-aligns to it. This walks that lane end to end against a finding staged `settled` on an analogy to a neighbouring rule — the derivation shape that used to ride auto straight into the specification — and holds it beside a call the record really does determine, so the dispose has to discriminate rather than blanket-hold.
conduct: The user is resuming their card-payments specification to run its review; construction finished last sitting, so offered the resume choice they continue. At the first finding — how long an order waits for capture confirmation — they see that the delivery schedule they already agreed settles it, and they choose auto, because they do not want to be stopped again for things the record has already decided. They know the discussion cold and treat what it determines as decided, not theirs to re-litigate. Shown a screen of calls made on their behalf, they read it, find the reasoning sound, and approve it as it stands — they pull nothing out to discuss and ask for nothing to be expanded. On an order the gateway never confirms they are clear whenever it comes up: they would not have the checkout cancel an order it cannot show failed, and they are content for a customer to be told the payment is still confirming. With auto set, the follow-up review cycle runs without asking them and comes back clean, and the session moves to completion on its own; at sign-off they confirm. Throughout they answer concretely and never reopen decided questions.
